before.label: English
before.title: The Late Prachi
stanzas: Had she brought only that much life,
or was some of it taken away?
that she was fortune's goddess for countless lives,
Whatever stone she stroked with affection
She could set time within a clay image,
she could give nature countless colours.
The sky practised austerities to touch her,
the earth prayed to become a mother.
So much glory, so much greatness—
mostly things heard; yet in what the eyes saw,
slowly she hastened toward death's river-mouth.
That she was dying, through metaphors and signs,
in love's legends, in memory's ocean,
Which anniversary of her death is today,
I fly about, circle and circle,
in the valley of her past.
